elements.name: The BIOS loader needs the flat kernel bytes,

runs.text: The BIOS loader needs the flat kernel bytes, not an ELF header.

Repository sources: build.sh. The build assembles ELF32 stubs, compiles freestanding C, links the kernel at 0x10000 and converts ELF to a flat binary. It computes the number of sectors for the bootloader and pads the image.

elements.name: Execution moves from 16-bit BIOS code to the

runs.text: Execution moves from 16-bit BIOS code to the 32-bit C kernel.

Repository sources: boot.asm; kernel/entry.asm; kernel/kernel.c. The loader uses BIOS INT 13h extensions, enables A20, loads the GDT, sets CR0.PE and jumps to 0x10000. Entry code initializes the stack and clears BSS.

elements.name: Then: login, network initialization, RAMFS i

runs.text: Then: login, network initialization, RAMFS initialization and shell

Repository sources: kernel/kernel.c. kmain initializes hardware, memory, interrupts and scheduler before showing the banner. login_run gates access. net_init follows login, then RAMFS initialization and the infinite shell loop.

elements.name: 4 KiB pages. A 16 KiB kernel stack. Files al

runs.text: 4 KiB pages. A 16 KiB kernel stack. Files allocate their contents from the heap.

Repository sources: linker.ld; kernel/entry.asm; kernel/memory/memory.c; kernel/memory/paging.c. The first 8 MiB are identity-mapped through two page tables of 1024 4 KiB pages. The heap spans 4–8 MiB. kfree checks and clears allocations but the allocator is a bump allocator with no general reuse.

elements.name: VGA text output displays the prompt, command

runs.text: VGA text output displays the prompt, command results and errors.

Repository sources: kernel/drivers/keyboard.c; kernel/drivers/vga.c; kernel/io/line_input.c; kernel/interrupts/pic.c. PIC remaps IRQ vectors and unmasks keyboard IRQ1. Network receive uses polling. VGA output writes text to the text buffer. The line-input helper supplies editable lines and controls echo.

Repository sources: kernel/shell/shell.c. Input capacity is 256 bytes and command capacity is 32 bytes, both including terminators. The current directory begins at /. Arguments are parsed by whitespace. This shell does not implement pipes or a full quoting language.

elements.name: Each file stores a normalized path, byte len

runs.text: Each file stores a normalized path, byte length and pointer to its contents.

Repository sources: kernel/fs/ramfs/ramfs.h; kernel/fs/ramfs/ramfs.c; kernel/fs/ramfs/path.h. The filesystem holds up to 96 entries. Each stores a used flag, node type, absolute path, data pointer and size. The path buffer is 128 bytes; validation can reject paths before full capacity. Root is implicit and lookup scans entries. Reboot discards the filesystem.

elements.name: File CRUD maps directly to RAMFS

runs.text: File CRUD maps directly to RAMFS

Repository sources: kernel/shell/shell.c; kernel/fs/ramfs/ramfs.c. Create rejects an existing path. Write creates or replaces a file and ensures parent directories. Reads use offset/capacity. Unlink refuses root and nonempty directories. These are kernel functions, not completed POSIX file descriptors.

elements.name: The shell handles text. RAMFS owns the file

runs.text: The shell handles text. RAMFS owns the file state.

Repository sources: kernel/shell/shell.c; kernel/fs/ramfs/ramfs.c. The shell splits path from remaining text and resolves an absolute path. RAMFS creates parents when needed, allocates new data before replacing existing data, and returns a status. The heap is finite.

elements.name: tcpping checks a listening TCP port with a S

runs.text: tcpping checks a listening TCP port with a SYN-ACK response.

Repository sources: kernel/net/ne2k.c; kernel/net/tcp_probe.c; kernel/net/net_config.h. NE2000 is configured at I/O 0x300 and IRQ11, while packet reception is polled. The probe builds Ethernet, ARP, IPv4 and TCP packets. It does not provide an HTTP or TLS client.

Repository sources: kernel/net/net_config.h; bochsrc.bxrc. These addresses are compiled defaults, not a guarantee that the selected Bochs network backend provides that subnet. Match them to the chosen network. Changing net_config.h requires a rebuild.
A successful probe establishes reachability, not Gemini API access.

Repository sources: kernel/net/tcp_probe.c. The next hop is the destination on the local subnet or the configured gateway. The probe broadcasts ARP, sends SYN, checks reply addresses, ports, flags and acknowledgement, then sends RST+ACK to end the probe. It does not transfer an application payload.

Repository sources: host_tools/tcp_ping/__main__.py; host_tools/tcp_ping/http_server.py; host_tools/tcp_ping/tcp_probe.py. The Python utility uses the host operating system TCP connect API. It is separate from the guest SYN probe. It serves /health, /status and GET/POST /ping on 127.0.0.1:8765 by default. No outbound probe occurs until requested.
